usage: everyday word; often shortened to 얘기 in speech
이야기 + 하다 means to have a conversation
examples: 들어요 is the 요-form of 듣다
nuance: 이야기 means both a "story" and "talking/chatting" in general. In daily conversation Koreans very often shorten it to 얘기, so 이야기해요 and 얘기해요 mean the same thing.
mistakes: Don't confuse 이야기 (story/talk) with 이아기.
이야기 is a noun, so to say "talk" you usually add 하다: 이야기하다.

usage: personal news, not TV news (that is 뉴스)
전하다 = to pass on, to convey
examples: I heard news about my friend.
There has been no word lately.
nuance: 소식 is news about a person or situation, like "how someone is doing." For TV or newspaper news Koreans usually say 뉴스. 소식이 없다 often means you haven't heard from someone in a while.
mistakes: Don't use 소식 for TV news; that is 뉴스.
Say 소식을 듣다 (hear news), not 소식을 보다.

examples: My younger sibling told a lie.
nuance: 거짓말 literally combines 거짓 (false) and 말 (words). To say "to lie," Koreans add 하다: 거짓말하다. Among close friends, 거짓말! can also mean "No way!" or "You're kidding!"
mistakes: 거짓말 is the noun; to lie you say 거짓말을 하다.
Don't confuse 거짓말 (lie) with 진짜 (real) or 사실 (truth).

usage: use to clarify you are not serious
nuance: 농담 is a light joke meant to be funny, not mean. If something might sound serious, Koreans add 농담이에요 to show they are kidding. The opposite, 진담, means you really mean it.
mistakes: 농담 is a noun; to joke, say 농담을 하다.
Saying 농담이에요 quickly after a remark softens it and shows you were not serious.

usage: to contact, to get in touch
examples: I got a message from my friend.
Please tell me your contact info.
알려 주세요 = please let me know
nuance: 연락 covers any way of reaching someone: calling, texting, or messaging. 연락하다 means "to contact," and 연락이 오다 means contact comes "to" you. 연락처 specifically means a phone number or contact details.
mistakes: Don't confuse 연락 (contact) with 연습 (practice).
Use 연락이 오다 for receiving contact, not 연락을 오다.

usage: asking someone to do something for you
polite way to start a request
please take care of it / nice to work with you
examples: I have one favor to ask.
Please take care of this for me.
I asked my friend for a favor.
nuance: 부탁 is asking someone to help or do something for you. 잘 부탁해요 (or the polite 잘 부탁드립니다) is a very common phrase when meeting new people or handing over work, roughly "please treat me/this kindly."
mistakes: 부탁 is a noun; to make a request, say 부탁을 하다 or 부탁하다.
잘 부탁드립니다 is more polite than 잘 부탁해요 for formal situations.

usage: written on paper, sent by mail
examples: I write a letter to my mom.
I received a letter from my friend.
I sent a letter for the birthday.
nuance: 편지 is a paper letter you write and mail. For email Koreans say 이메일, and for a short text they say 문자. Writing a 손편지 (handwritten letter) is seen as warm and personal.
mistakes: Use 쓰다 (write) with 편지, not 만들다 (make).
Don't confuse 편지 (letter) with 편의점 (convenience store).

usage: answer to a letter, text, or email
nuance: 답장 is a reply to something written, like a letter, text, or email. It is different from 대답, which is answering a spoken question. 답장이 없다 means someone has not written back yet.
mistakes: Use 답장 for written replies and 대답 for spoken answers.
답장 is a noun; to reply, say 답장을 하다 or 답장하다.

nuance: 단어 is a vocabulary word, the kind you study and memorize. 말 is broader and means "words/speech" in general. When learning Korean you will hear 단어 a lot in class and study apps.
mistakes: Don't confuse 단어 (vocabulary word) with 단오 or 단원.
For "meaning of a word" say 단어의 뜻, using 뜻.

nuance: 발음 means how words are pronounced. Korean learners often say 발음이 어려워요 because some sounds are new. A compliment you will hear a lot is 발음이 좋아요 (your pronunciation is good).
mistakes: 발음 is a noun; to pronounce something, say 발음하다.
Say 발음이 좋다 (pronunciation is good), not 발음을 좋다.

examples: I feel good because I got praise.
nuance: 칭찬 is a kind word said about someone's good action or quality. 칭찬을 받다 (receive praise) and 칭찬을 듣다 (hear praise) are both common. The opposite is 야단 or 혼나다 (being scolded).
mistakes: 칭찬 is a noun; to compliment, say 칭찬을 하다 or 칭찬하다.
Use 칭찬을 받다/듣다 for receiving a compliment, not 칭찬을 가지다.

usage: telling how or why something works
examples: I listened to the explanation well.
한 번 더 = one more time
nuance: 설명 is an explanation of how or why something is. To explain, add 하다: 설명하다, often softened as 설명해 주세요 (please explain for me). It pairs naturally with 듣다 (hear) and 하다 (do).
mistakes: 설명 is a noun; to explain, use 설명하다.
Don't confuse 설명 (explanation) with 설탕 (sugar).

usage: a greeting asking how someone is
examples: Please give my regards to your parents.
My friend asked how I was doing.
I send regards to your family.
nuance: 안부 is asking or sharing how someone is doing. 안부를 전하다 means "please pass along my regards," and 안부를 묻다 means to ask after someone's well-being. It is a warm, polite way to show you care.
mistakes: Use 전하다 (pass on) or 묻다 (ask) with 안부, not 하다 alone.
안부를 전하다 means "give my regards (to someone else)"; to ask after them directly, use 안부를 묻다.
